# Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions possible)

Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Project tests must pass at the end.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

## Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

## API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `<id>` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `<id>` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `<id>` is not a positive integ

`/api/bookings?date=<value>` and `/api/bookings/<id>`.
- A reply has an error status when its status is not the success status of its request: 200 for `GET`, 201 for `POST` and 204 for `DELETE`. The reply's error message is the body's `error` value when the body is a JSON object whose `error` is a string, and `Request failed.` otherwise. A reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read or parsed as JSON counts as no reply. A request that gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.

When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.

The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` — frontend. The script must work against the API exactly as in the spec note.
- `test/*.test.mjs` — testing. `package.json` test script: `node --test test/`.
- `package.json` — backend creates it: `{"name":"room-bookings","type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`.
- `README.md` — docs.

{
  "name": "room-bookings",
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node server.mjs",
    "test": "node --test test/"
  }
}

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
The server matches the spec on every point I checked and passes: 9.1/10 overall, with no item under 9 (tests are n/a). I read `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs` (324 lines) and `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/package.json` against the spec and layout notes. The project has no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or `.claude/rules`, so I graded against the house rules. `node --check` passes. No tests exist yet, which is expected.

**Matches the spec:**
- **Startup order:** PORT is checked first (line 303), then the data file is read (307), then the server listens (316).
- **PORT rules:** unset or empty means 3000, only ASCII digits are accepted, values above 65535 are rejected, and `PORT=0` is allowed. The listening line on stdout uses the port actually bound and is the only stdout write.
- **DATA_FILE:** relative paths resolve against the current working directory. A missing file (`ENOENT`) means no bookings; any other read error, invalid JSON or unknown layout writes `cannot read data file <name as given>` and exits 1. The file is checked strictly: exact keys, unique ids below `nextId`, no overlaps.
- **Saving:** state is set only after `writeFile` succeeds (lines 104-105), so a failed save leaves both the bookings and the next id unchanged and the reply is 500. Changes run one at a time through a promise queue, and the queue survives a failed task (111).
- **Request body:** the whole body is read before any route runs, so the 413 and 415 replies arrive. Only up to 10001 bytes are kept, but all received bytes are counted. Rules 1-10 run in spec order: 415, 413, 400 for a non-object body, then the field checks, then 409 with the earliest overlapping booking.
- **Routing:** paths are compared byte for byte up to the first `?`. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` give 404. HEAD and OPTIONS give 405. A bad DELETE id gives 404 `booking not found` before the queue is used.
- **Replies and package.json:** Content-Type values are exact, and 204 has no body. A failure reading the page files gives 500. `package.json` matches the layout note exactly.

**Small problems:**
- **Line 50:** `isValidTitle` calls `value.trim()` twice. Trim once into a local.
- **Line 204:** the sort comparator never returns 0 and duplicates the start comparison in `compareBookings`. Use `a.start.localeCompare(b.start)`, or a small `byStart` helper shared with `compareBookings`.
- **Lines 177-182:** `let bookings` is reassigned. A `const` with a conditional filter fits the immutability rule better.
- **Lines 296-299 and 312-314:** the server-error handler calls `fail()`, which sets `process.exitCode`, and then calls `process.exit(1)` anyway. Have `fail` either always exit or never exit.
- **Line 313:** the port error prints the raw code, e.g. `cannot listen on port 3000: EADDRINUSE`. Map `EADDRINUSE` and `EACCES` to plain messages such as `port 3000 is already in use` (spec-compliant either way).
- **Line 104 (optional):** `writeFile` overwrites the file in place, so a crash mid-write could leave a corrupt file that blocks the next startup. Writing a temp file in the same folder and renaming it over the original avoids this; the spec doesn't require it.
- **Line 55:** `typeof body.room !== 'string'` is redundant, since `ROOMS.includes` already rejects non-strings.

**For the testing section:** tests a wrong implementation would fail:
- PORT values `65535` and `65536`, `' 80'` and `'+80'`.
- A data file path that is a directory, and an empty data file.
- The 10000-byte vs 10001-byte body edge.
- Media type with surrounding tabs and mixed case.
- `?date` with no value.
- DELETE `/api/bookings/01`.
- An overlap where one booking ends exactly when another starts, which must be allowed.
- Feb 29 in 2100 vs 2096, and February 2000.

## GRADE
Overall: 9.1/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — clear sections, small single-purpose functions, state replaced not mutated; minor `let` reassignment in listBookings and mixed exitCode/exit in fail
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent; `q`/`b` short locals are acceptable in context
duplication: 9 — start-time comparison duplicated between line 204 and compareBookings; double trim in isValidTitle
size: 10 — 324-line file, longest function (route) about 28 lines
errors: 9 — ENOENT vs other errors told apart, exact spec messages, one-line stderr plus exit 1, 500 without leaks; EADDRINUSE shows a raw code rather than a plain sentence
tests: n/a — written later by the testing section
security: 10 — no secrets, fixed static whitelist (no path traversal), body capped, JSON output only
leftovers: 9 — no console.log or debug code; only section-divider comments
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:50 trim once into a local instead of calling value.trim() twice
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:204 replace the never-zero comparator with a shared byStart helper (or localeCompare) reused by compareBookings
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:177 use a const with a conditional filter instead of reassigning `let bookings`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:296 make fail() consistently exit or not; drop the redundant process.exit(1) pairing at 314/323 or the exitCode set
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:313 map EADDRINUSE/EACCES to plain one-line messages (e.g. "port 3000 is already in use")
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:55 drop the redundant typeof check; ROOMS.includes already rejects non-strings
- /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:104 (optional) write to a temp file in the same folder and rename it, so a crash mid-write cannot corrupt the data file
